blocks.text: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons and mostly undergo electrophilic addition reactions. Other, minor types include oxidation, combustion and polymerisation. The addition reactions and their mechanisms are treated in 11.8.1.

blocks.prompt: Explain the difference between an addition and an elimination reaction, and why addition increases the saturation of a molecule (Quick Check 11.7b, 11.9ii; exercise Q.2d).
blocks.explanation: In addition a small molecule adds across a double bond, which opens to two single bonds, so the product has more atoms attached to the carbons and no multiple bond: it is more saturated. Elimination is the reverse: a small molecule such as water or HBr is removed from adjacent carbons to create a double bond. Dehydration of ethanol gives ethene; hydration of ethene gives ethanol back.

items: Alkenes mainly undergo electrophilic addition; also oxidation, combustion and polymerisation.
